_about: The setup wizard's questions and the gear CasaTorch supports. Each option says how it is set up: 'ha' = CasaTorch runs that integration's own setup inside Home Assistant (HA asks its questions, CasaTorch shows them); 'ha-ui' = needs a sign-in page that only Home Assistant can show (OAuth), so CasaTorch opens it there; 'direct' = CasaTorch talks to it itself; 'guide' = instructions only. Add gear here - no code needed for an 'ha' option. 'hue' / 'ring' = CasaTorch's own pairing or sign-in screens. 'haTwin' names the Home Assistant option that does the same job: when Home Assistant is connected the HA one is shown, otherwise this one.

steps.title: Your home
steps.intro: A few basics so times, temperatures, costs and the weather show the way you expect.

fields.label: What should we call your home?
Your town (for the weather) - already set on the first page if you chose it there

steps.title: Your CasaTorch login
steps.intro: Your own sign-in for CasaTorch. You'll use it on phones and other screens; later you can add family members, turn on two-step sign-in, or connect Google sign-in in Settings > Security.

fields.label: Password (10+ characters - a short sentence works well)
CasaTorch Pro license key (optional)
fields.help: Every new CasaTorch gets 14 days of Pro free. Already bought Pro? Paste the key from your e-mail.

fields.label: I have read and agree to the Terms of Use and the Privacy Notice.

steps.title: Your phone
steps.intro: The login you just made is this CasaTorch's owner - the main admin that is always here, for this screen and Settings. Now make a login for your phone, so the CasaTorch app (iPhone, iPad, Android) signs in as you without using the owner login. At the end of setup, scan a QR code with the app and the phone is signed in - no typing.

question.label: Sign in on your phone with...
options: A login just for my phone (recommended)

new.note: This login can change things in the house but can't remove the owner. Two-step sign-in is offered on the phone - we recommend it. Everything is stored on this CasaTorch, encrypted - never in a CasaTorch cloud.

fields.label: Phone login password
fields.help: At least 10 characters - a short sentence works well. Stored only as a salted scrypt hash on this CasaTorch.

fields.label: Use the app away from home too?
fields.help: CasaTorch gets its own secure https address through an encrypted outbound tunnel - no router changes, no open ports. Every request still needs your sign-in. It's encrypted (https) between your phone and Cloudflare, which runs the tunnel, and between Cloudflare and your CasaTorch; CasaTorch's own servers aren't in the path and keep nothing. From anywhere is part of Pro (in your 14-day trial); on Basic it works on your home Wi-Fi.

owner.note: Your phone will use the owner login. Turning on two-step sign-in for it is strongly recommended.

steps.title: Calendars
steps.intro: Show your family's schedule on the Home screen. CasaTorch has its own calendar you can fill in right in the app - no Google account needed. If you already use Google, iCloud or Outlook, you can also link those.

fields.label: Use the CasaTorch calendar (add events in the app)

steps.help: Google: calendar.google.com > Settings > your calendar > Integrate calendar > Secret address in iCal format. iCloud: Calendar app > share icon next to the calendar > Public Calendar > copy link. Outlook: Settings > Calendar > Shared calendars > Publish a calendar > ICS link.

steps.title: Your teams
steps.intro: Live scores and the next game for the teams you follow.

steps.title: Headlines
steps.intro: Headlines on your Home screen: local, national and world news for where you live, in your language - plus topics and any sources you like.

steps.title: Reminders
steps.intro: Your home's own reminders - trash night, meds, feeding the fish, a birthday. At the right time they light up every screen with an icon and a sound; later you can add a photo, and with Pro send them to everyone's phone.

steps.title: Your Home AI Agent
steps.intro: Your Home AI Agent knows your home: ask "Is anything still on downstairs?", "What's using all the power?" or "Will it rain for trash night?" and get a straight answer - with a button to do it. It never unlocks doors, opens the garage or disarms the alarm, and anything it switches, you confirm first. Part of Pro (included in your 14-day trial); the AI company bills its own usage, usually cents a month.

question.label: Which AI should power your Home AI Agent?

fields.help: Stored only on your CasaTorch, sealed with AES-256-GCM - never sent to CasaTorch's servers. It goes only to the AI company you picked, when you ask something.

fields.label: OpenAI API key

ollama.note: Fully private: the questions never leave your home. Needs a computer with a good graphics card running Ollama.

later.note: Add it any time in Settings › Home AI Agent.

guides.install-ha:
The easiest way, no computer skills needed: get a Home Assistant Green, a small box made by the Home Assistant team. Plug it into your router and power, wait five minutes, then open http://homeassistant.local:8123 on your phone or computer and follow its welcome screens to make your account.

Already have a spare computer or a Raspberry Pi? Home Assistant's website has a one-click installer for those too: home-assistant.io/installation

When Home Assistant shows its dashboard, come back here and choose 'Yes'. CasaTorch takes it from there - you just sign in with your Home Assistant account.
guides.wyze: Wyze cameras work through docker-wyze-bridge, which turns them into normal streams. Install it, then pick 'Frigate' or 'Other IP camera'.
guides.cloud-cams: Arlo and Eufy are cloud cameras. Add them in Home Assistant with the community integrations (HACS); CasaTorch shows them once they're there.
guides.already-in-ha: Anything already in Home Assistant shows up in CasaTorch automatically - nothing else to do.
guides.emporia: Emporia Vue works through a community integration (HACS). Add it in Home Assistant; CasaTorch reads it from there.
guides.meraki-soon: Pick Cisco Meraki and paste your API key right here.
